notes: Recognized the paper title from prior knowledge but did not use any knowledge of reviews or outcome. The skill was followable. Friction: (1) the paper type has no exact 'dataset+benchmark' choice, I chose benchmark; (2) the Phase 1.5 order (literature check after drafting the reports) conflicts with the practical need to know the closest prior works while writing the Domain report, and scores.json had to be fixed before the reports were written out; (3) related_search.py rejects hyphenated words as multiple words (e.g. multi-file counts as two), which makes 4-word queries awkward; (4) the 'benchmarks' command returned nothing for a paper that is itself a benchmark, so the baseline-scout step was largely vacuous; (5) Multi-SWE-bench, which the paper cites, was labelled 'recent preprint' by its v1 date, so the label system cannot tell that the paper cites it; (6) the composite cross-check (band 3) disagreed with the rating-based starting point (4) near a boundary, and the EIC rule says not to depart without a named verified issue, which was followed; (7) ICLR rating label was returned in two scales and is not a single label; (8) all five reviewers share one context, so independence is limited and disclosed; (9) the helper tools and shell variables are restricted in this environment, so searches were run one per command.
